# nagios_nna_check (Resource)

Manages a Nagios Network Analyzer alert check - a warning/critical threshold evaluated against a metric on a flow source or source group. This is Network Analyzer's closest analog to a Nagios XI service check.

Only Network Analyzer's `flow_source` check type is currently supported. Network Analyzer also has `nmap`, `suricata` and `system` checks, each targeting a different kind of object with its own metric set; those are tracked in issue #225 and are not manageable through this resource yet.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nagios_nna_source" "core_switch" {
  name        = "core-switch-netflow"
  port        = 9995
  flowtype    = "netflow"
  lifetime    = "30"
  description = "NetFlow export from the core switch"
}

# Alert when HTTPS traffic from the core switch gets unusually heavy.
resource "nagios_nna_check" "https_volume" {
  name        = "core-switch-https-volume"
  object_type = "source"
  object_id   = nagios_nna_source.core_switch.id

  metric             = "bps"
  warning_threshold  = "100000000"
  critical_threshold = "500000000"

  queries = [{
    location       = "destination"
    location_type  = "port"
    location_bool  = "is"
    location_value = "443"
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `metric` (String) The flow metric to evaluate the thresholds against. One of `bytes`, `flows`, `packets`, `pps`, `bps`, `bpp`, or `abnormal_behavior`. Thresholds are ignored for `abnormal_behavior`.
- `name` (String) The name of this check.
- `object_id` (Number) The ID of the `nagios_nna_source` or `nagios_nna_source_group` this check evaluates. Network Analyzer does not validate this reference, so an ID that doesn't exist is accepted on write and simply yields a check that never produces a result - prefer interpolating another resource's `id` over hardcoding a number.
- `object_type` (String) What `object_id` refers to: `source` for a single flow source, or `sourcegroup` for a source group.

### Optional

- `alert_commands` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer commands to run when this check changes state.
- `alert_nagios_servers` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer Nagios server definitions to send passive check results to.
- `alert_snmp_receivers` (Set of Number) IDs of Network Analyzer SNMP trap receivers to notify.
- `alert_users` (Set of Number) IDs of `nagios_nna_user` accounts to notify when this check changes state.
- `check_type` (String) The kind of object this check evaluates. Only `flow_source` is supported by this provider today, so this attribute rarely needs setting.
- `critical_threshold` (String) The critical threshold, in Nagios range syntax. Same conventions as `warning_threshold`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this check is actively evaluated. A newly created check always starts enabled, since Network Analyzer ignores this on create; set to false to have Terraform disable it immediately afterwards.
- `queries` (Attributes List) Traffic filter clauses narrowing what this check measures. Network Analyzer compiles these server-side into the `raw_query` filter expression below and never returns them, so - unlike every other attribute here - changes made outside Terraform to the underlying filter cannot be detected; `raw_query` is the observable result of what was last applied. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--queries))
- `warning_threshold` (String) The warning threshold, in Nagios range syntax (e.g. `1000`, `10:20`, `~:500`, `@10:20`). Omit the attribute entirely for no warning threshold - Network Analyzer stores an empty threshold as null and would report it back as unset, so an explicitly empty string is rejected here rather than causing a permanent diff.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric ID Network Analyzer assigns this check. Unlike this provider's XI resources, Network Analyzer addresses objects by ID rather than name.
- `last_code` (Number) The Nagios return code from the last run (0 OK, 1 warning, 2 critical, 3 unknown). Null until it first runs.
- `last_output` (String) The status text from the last run. Empty until it first runs.
- `last_run` (String) When this check last ran. Empty until it first runs.
- `last_value` (String) The metric value recorded the last time this check ran. Empty until it first runs.
- `raw_query` (String) The traffic filter expression Network Analyzer compiled from `queries` (e.g. `src port 443`). Read-only.

<a id="nestedatt--queries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `queries`

Required:

- `location` (String) Which end of the flow to match: `source`, `destination`, or `destination_or_source`.
- `location_bool` (String) Whether the clause matches (`is`) or excludes (`is_not`).
- `location_type` (String) What kind of value to match: `port`, `ip`, or `network`.
- `location_value` (String) The value to match - a port number, an IPv4 address, or a CIDR network, according to `location_type`.
